explanation: `count++` looks like a single operation but is actually three steps: read `count`, add 1, write it back. When multiple threads call `increment()` concurrently, two threads can both read the same value before either writes its incremented result back, so one of the increments is silently lost. Without synchronization (a `synchronized` method, a lock, or an `AtomicInteger`), `count` will end up lower than the number of increment calls under concurrent access.
